Package org.cibseven.connect.ai.agent.impl

Class AdHocResults

java.lang.Object
org.cibseven.connect.ai.agent.impl.AdHocResults
public final class AdHocResults extends Object
What the agent is told finished since it last looked: one entry per performance of a tool, taken as the child ends and kept on the agent state until it has been shown.

Taken as the child ends, because that is the one moment its declared variables still hold what this performance produced: two runs of one tool leave one set of variables, and reading them at the next step would show the second twice or the first never. The scope's behaviour says when that moment is (AdHocSubProcessObserver), so nothing is installed into the scope's outputCollection; that belongs to the modeller (CIB7-2147).

Kept on the agent state, a sibling of the tools, so no tool can rewrite what the agent is told, and one per scope execution, so two agents, the instances of a multi-instance agent and a scope entered again each see only their own. The list goes with the scope.

A tool that holds its results in an execution of its own loses them before its child ends; carry(org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.persistence.entity.ExecutionEntity) keeps them on the child's execution as the tool ends, and the child's end takes them into the list (CIB7-2215). An entry is still written only there.

Each entry is a variable of its own on the agent state, adHocAgentResults~<n> with its position in the list padded with zeros to ten digits, written once as its child ends and never again (CIB7-2156). The list was one variable rewritten whole on every child's end, so at history level full each end stored every entry before it once more: quadratic in the performances. A list an earlier version wrote, adHocAgentResults without a suffix, is still read, before the entries; nothing writes it any more.

Only a child that ends writes an entry; a step moves a read position and records what a tool result already showed, both in the agent's state map, which only a step writes. A child ending while a step waits for the model therefore meets no row the step changes, and neither has to be repeated (T01). Two children ending at once take the same next position: the second insert fails on the engine's unique index of variable names (ACT_UNIQ_VARIABLE), as the second update of the one list failed before. Run in a job, its transaction is retried and appends after the first; a task completed through the API gets the exception, as it did then.

A step that reads the entries must not write them either. The engine serializes an object it read again when the command ends, and writes it back if the bytes differ; a hash map can come back with a different table size, on Java 17 at twelve entries and every doubling of that. So every map in an entry is a TreeMap, whose bytes depend only on what it holds, and an entry is built that way when it is written.

  • Method Details

    • gather

      public static void gather(ExecutionEntity scope, ExecutionEntity ended)
      Records what the child ended of the agentic scope scope produced: the values of the variables its tool declares, made safe for a prompt now, while they still hold this performance's values. A child that is not one of the scope's tools records nothing.

      The tool is the one the agent called for this performance, looked up by the child's execution (CIB7-2147), so a chain along inner flows is reported under its first activity, with where it ended. A child someone else started is looked up by its activity. A multi-instance tool ends once, as its multi-instance body, after its last instance (CIB7-2153): it is reported under the activity the agent called, with the values its declared variables hold then.

    • removed

      public static void removed(ExecutionEntity scope, ExecutionEntity removed)
      Records that the child removed of the agentic scope scope was removed without ending: cancelled from outside, by a process instance modification (CIB7-2166). Its variables are gone; only which tool it was, and the activity its execution was at, are read. The agent is told, so it does not go on waiting for it. A child that is not one of the scope's tools records nothing.

      That activity says little for sure. At the tool itself, the tool did not complete, unless it had and only waited for its asyncAfter job, which is where an incident leaves it and an operator cancels it. At an activity further along the chain, inside the scope itself, the tool ran when it has no boundary events: only its completion leads there. With one, an error path may have led there, so it may not have done its work. An activity inside the tool, a sub process, is no sign it ran. And an execution at a scope, which every activity with a boundary event is, carries no activity at all. So the tool itself without asyncAfter is taken as "did not complete", an activity further along the chain of a tool without boundary events as "ran"; everywhere else the model is told the activity, if known, and that whether the work took effect is open (see describeEnd(java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object>, java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object>)).

    • recordInterruption

      public static void recordInterruption(ExecutionEntity execution, String boundaryEventId, String attachedTo, String eventType, String errorCode, String exceptionClass)
      Records on the performance execution belongs to that the interrupting boundary event boundaryEventId, attached to attachedTo, of kind eventType, interrupted its flow; for an error, with the code it caught, and for a Java exception mapped to one, the class thrown (CIB7-2166). An execution outside every agentic scope, or on the event scope of one that has left, records nothing.

      The performance is the agentic scope's child the execution runs under, the one the activation created and the scope's observer is told about. The interruption is added to those recorded before; one of the same activity, which a retry did not repair, is replaced, since the newer one is how that activity ended.

    • forgetInterruption

      public static void forgetInterruption(ExecutionEntity execution, String attachedTo)
      Forgets an interruption of the activity attachedTo recorded on the performance execution belongs to, as that activity completes in it (CIB7-2166): an event's path led back to it, and this time it did its work. Only that repairs the interruption. A flow that goes back to before it and ends without completing it again still reports it, and so does a retry that is still running. An interruption of another activity stays, also when this one was on that activity's own path.

    • carry

      public static void carry(ExecutionEntity toolScope)
      Carries what a tool that holds variables of its own declares as its result and holds there only, as its execution ends (CIB7-2215). An embedded sub process whose input parameter creates its result variable, for one: by the time the agentic scope is told the tool ended, the sub process's scope execution and its variables are gone, and gather(org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.persistence.entity.ExecutionEntity, org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.persistence.entity.ExecutionEntity) would read null. Likewise each instance of a multi-instance task with an input parameter, or of a multi-instance call activity with camunda:out local: the instance's execution is no scope, but its variables go with it.

      Called at the end of the tool's own execution, while its variables are still there. The values, made safe for a prompt as gather makes them, are kept on the execution the activation created, where gather reads them: in this transaction or, after an asyncAfter, in the next. That execution goes with the tool, so nothing reaches the process's variables. Only a value the tool's scope holds itself is carried; one found higher up is still there for gather. Nor is a name the tool's own output parameter writes: that mapping runs after this, as the scope is destroyed, and what it hands out of the scope is what gather is to read. Of a multi-instance tool, the value of the last instance that held the name locally is what is kept.

      A tool that is cancelled carries nothing: one interrupted by a boundary event reports what a lookup finds, as before the carrier.

      Each value is kept with what a lookup from the activation's execution showed for its name at that moment. A chain that goes on after the tool, along an inner flow, may write the name again; the lookup then shows the newer value, and gather reports that one instead of the carried one.
